Betreff:
ODP: reasons for charging session with 0kW (+precond?)
Hello,
In this case, during this session, the charger did not supply energy to the vehicle and the vehicle self-discharged 2 KW/h from 18% to 14% SOC.
Vehicle status and charging is Status C Current demand  but no current flows - problem on the charger side
Were two dispensers connected from one charger in this case? Is Sequential charging active with 2 - Dispensers ?
I saw such behavior of the Siemens charger during sequential charging in Switzerland.
Both Plug-INs are in the C current demand state, but only dispenser 1 - current flows and the second is also in the C current demand state, but current does not flow.
Plug-in no. 2 waits until the Vehicle connected to Plug-in no. 1 finishes charging.
Hubert Dreger
Starszy Inżynier Serwisowy ds. e-Mobility | Senior Service Engineer for e-Mobility
E-Mobility After Sales |
M: +48 691997345

additional_info.subject: 0400060 - ID0400060-DC/Si-D/NO-[BAobBx] 0kWh session CRM:00314000142
additional_info.body:
Good evening Benjamin,
I am reaching out from ES Team in regards of ticket
ID0400060.
The ticket was opened regarding charger
BAobBx
, for an event of no current flow with a Solaris eBus.
I analyzed the logs of the event with
TransactionID: 664181268.
Here is a summary of my findings:
Outlet DC2 was connected at 2025-01-13T11:58:38 and the charging process initialization started.
At 2025-01-13T11:59:15, the OCPP Start Transaction command was sent, with TransactionID: 664181268
However, right after the beginning of the charging session, at 2025-01-13T11:59:20 the charger reported an issue on the feedback of the auxiliary contactor of the outgoing coils QA13-14, which went to off while the command was off.
Due to this failure, the charger was not able to deliver current.
Only at 2025-01-13T13:50:46 the session was stopped by the EV.
I performed a screening of the charger and this failure of OutgoingCoil QA13-14 happened only in that occasion, so it is considered from our side a single failure event.
Even if the charger was unable to deliver current, it is the EV that can stop the charging session if, as in this case, no current is delivered by the Charger after Current demand from the EV. This is regulated by the standards in regards of output current regulation. As a matter of fact, if the Charger cannot follow the request of current coming from the EV, it is the EV that should stop the charging session.
I hope my reply has provided clarification. If you do not require any further information, I will proceed to close this ticket then.
With kind regards,
